# Bubba's Infused Gems: balance model

Generated by `tools/gem-balance.py` from the owner's design in `specs/effect-gems.md`. Do not edit by hand: change the script and rerun it. Vanilla numbers come from the decompiled Minecraft 26.3 source and the script re-checks them against it.

## The formula in plain words

- **A gem doesn't care where it goes** (owner). Every gem, from any potion, item or loot, fits armor (3 slots a piece) or a weapon (2 slots). **The slot decides who its effects reach:** in armor, the wearer; in a weapon, what it hits (bows and crossbows: the arrow). All of a gem's effects go the same way: main effect, any other effect and any drawback. So a Poison gem in your armor poisons you, and a Regeneration gem on a sword heals the target: allowed, just pointless.
- **There is one Infused Gem item** (owner); the base gem it was brewed from is its **Infusion level**: Infusion I (amethyst), Infusion II (quartz), Infusion III (ender pearl), Infusion IV (diamond), Infusion V (prismarine shard), Infusion VI (nether star). Names read like *Infused Gem: Infusion III, Speed (Splash)*.
- Every effect has **two curves on one scale**, 1.0 = the strongest vanilla level. **Worn** (armor): the effect on the wearer all the time, 1.0 = the strongest level of the effect (Speed II, Strength II, Resistance IV...), on/off effects made partial. **Hit-applied** (weapon): what one hit gives the target, 1.0 = what the strongest vanilla tipped arrow of that effect applies. Healing has its own, flatter worn curve.
- **One gem's strength** = potion factor x Infusion factor x enchant grade x gear factor. In armor the gear factor is armor material x matching run; in a weapon it is the weapon's material. Each is at most 1.0.
- **Armor stacking:** a piece holds 3 gems, so 12 in all. The gems of one effect are lined up strongest first; the first counts fully, each next one 85% of the one before. The sum is scaled so that 12 perfect gems give exactly **0.95**.
- **Weapon stacking:** a weapon holds 2 gems, same rule, scaled so 2 perfect gems give exactly **0.95**. One perfect gem gives 0.514: two gems of one effect, or one gem each of two effects.
- **The cap is 0.95**: 5% short of vanilla's best. Only the single best build reaches it: **lingering potion + Infusion VI (nether star) + tier 3 + full contiguous netherite** (armor), or **+ a netherite weapon with both slots** (weapons).
- **Potion form doesn't multiply**: it sets the highest enchant tier (normal 1, splash 2, lingering 3), and the tier sets the grade. So lingering is needed for the strongest grade.
- **Infusion level changes strength only** (owner): no traits. Order, by how hard the base gem is to get: amethyst, quartz, ender pearl, diamond, prismarine shard, nether star.
- **One roll table per gem** (owner): its main effect, maybe an **other** effect of the same kind (a beneficial gem's bonus is another beneficial effect, a harmful gem's another harmful one, never the main effect itself), maybe a **drawback** of the opposite kind that is **never the main effect's direct opposite**. The other effect uses the same formula with its own grade and joins that effect's stack; a drawback is a fixed, mild size (below).

Total for an effect, in symbols: `total = 0.95 x sum(gem_i x 0.85^(rank_i)) / sum(0.85^0..0.85^(slots-1))`, with `gem = potion x infusion x grade x gear`.

### Potion form -> highest enchant tier (owner)

| Form | Highest tier | Best grade reachable |
|---|---|---|
| Normal | 1 | weak |
| Splash | 2 | medium |
| Lingering | 3 | strongest |

The form is the potion's form, fixed at brewing; nothing raises it later (owner: potion -> gem, no other pathway). An item has no splash or lingering form, so an Infused Gem brewed from an item is normal form and reaches tier 1 at most; that gap is accepted.

### Weapon material (proposal: a factor, like armor)

Yes for consistency: the same gem is stronger in a better weapon, exactly as in better armor, so a netherite weapon is part of the single best build. Swords, axes and spears come in every material. Bows, crossbows, tridents and maces have none, so they get a fixed diamond-level factor: they can't be upgraded, and at diamond-level the best build stays unique to netherite.

## Every status effect: craftable, found-only, or not a gem

Every one of the 40 status effects in 26.3 (the script reads them from the source and fails if one is missing). Any gem goes into armor or a weapon. An effect with a potion is brewed from it. One without a potion is brewed from a vanilla item that already carries it: in 26.3 the brewing stand's bottle slot takes any item that a brewing recipe names as its input (BrewingStandMenu.PotionSlot asks the recipes, PotionIngredient.isPotionInput), so this is data, no menu change. Stews are told apart by their stew effect with Fabric API's components ingredient. An effect with no sensible item is a **found-only** gem: loot and mob gear, never brewed.

| Effect | Kind | How it's had |
|---|---|---|

### Found-only gems: what they come with

A found gem is made as if brewed and enchanted: its potion factor is 1.0 (one form of the effect), its Infusion level is picked from the loot source's list and its tier rolled from the source's tiers with the normal tier odds. Same strength scale as crafted gems; only ominous loot can give a perfect one.

| Loot source | Infusion levels | Tiers | Strength range (gem quality) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Common loot (mineshafts, dungeons, shipwrecks, fishing treasure, hero gifts) | Infusion I (amethyst), Infusion II (quartz), Infusion III (ender pearl) | 1, 2 | 0.40 - 0.66 (or a drawback-only roll at tier 1) |
| Rare loot (strongholds, ancient cities, end cities, buried treasure, outposts) | Infusion IV (diamond), Infusion V (prismarine shard) | 2, 3 | 0.69 - 0.96 |
| Ominous vaults in trial chambers (and the elder guardian for Mining Fatigue) | Infusion V (prismarine shard), Infusion VI (nether star) | 3 | 0.96 - 1.00 |

## Roll tables

One roll table per gem, whatever slot it later goes into. **Other** (tier 2 weak, tier 3 weak or medium): any gem effect of the main effect's kind except itself and the main-effect-only ones (Healing: its own per-hit curve: main effect only; Harming: a charged strike: main effect only; Hero of the Village: a permanent villager discount stays a rare found gem: main effect only). **Drawback** (tier 1 alone, tier 3 with the strongest main effect): one of the opposite kind, never the main effect's direct opposite.

### Direct opposites (never a drawback of each other)

| Beneficial | Harmful | Why they cancel out |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | Slowness | movement speed up / down (owner) |
| Strength | Weakness | attack damage up / down (owner) |
| Haste | Mining Fatigue | mining and attack speed up / down (owner) |
| Regeneration | Poison | health over time back / away (owner) |
| Regeneration | Wither | health over time back / away (owner) |
| Luck | Bad Luck | luck +1 / -1 (owner) |
| Healing | Harming | instant heal / instant damage (owner) |
| Saturation | Hunger | food kept / food drained (owner) |
| Night Vision | Blindness | sight in the dark / no sight (owner) |
| Night Vision | Darkness | sight in the dark / pulsing dark (owner) |
| Invisibility | Glowing | hidden / outlined through walls (owner) |
| Slow Falling | Levitation | slower fall / forced rise (owner) |
| Conduit Power | Mining Fatigue | added: Conduit Power's underwater mining is the conduit's Haste, and Mining Fatigue is the ocean monument's direct answer to it |

Checked and left out (no direct opposite in vanilla): **Jump Boost**: no vanilla effect lowers jumps; Slow Falling / Levitation is a different axis (falling, not jumping); **Resistance (from Turtle Master)**: no vanilla effect raises damage taken; Weakness lowers damage dealt, which is Strength's opposite; **Health Boost**: no vanilla effect lowers max health; Wither drains health over time, which is Regeneration's opposite; **Absorption**: no vanilla effect takes absorption away; same reasoning as Health Boost; **Fire Resistance**: no vanilla effect makes fire hurt more; **Water Breathing**: no vanilla effect drains air faster; **Dolphin's Grace**: no vanilla effect slows swimming alone; Slowness is Speed's opposite; **Hero of the Village**: its opposite is Bad Omen, which is not a gem or a drawback. Harmful effects with no beneficial counterpart: Nausea, Wind Charged, Weaving, Oozing, Infested.

### Drawback candidates

A beneficial gem's drawback rolls from: Slowness, Weakness, Mining Fatigue, Hunger, Bad Luck. A harmful gem's drawback rolls from: Speed, Regeneration, Resistance (from Turtle Master), Jump Boost. Minus the main effect's direct opposite, which leaves every gem at least 3 candidates. Never a drawback: Poison (a permanent damage-over-time on the wearer cancels natural healing and nags at every moment; it can't kill but pins the wearer near 1 HP); Wither (the same as poison, and it can kill); Harming (instant, no mild form); Blindness (ruins the screen, not just the gem); Darkness (ruins the screen, not just the gem); Nausea (ruins the screen, not just the gem); Levitation (dangerous, not mild); Glowing (harmless alone, a beacon in PvP); Wind Charged (only felt at death); Weaving (only felt at death); Oozing (only felt at death); Infested (spawns mobs, not mild); Absorption (changes the fight too much); Health Boost (changes the fight too much); Strength (changes the fight too much); Invisibility (the target vanishes); Fire Resistance (would cancel Fire Aspect).

|---|---|---|---|---|

## In armor: what each gem does to the wearer

Beneficial gems are what armor is for. Harmful gems in armor hit the wearer (pointless, but allowed): damage-over-time and attribute effects at the same level as their hit anchor, on/off effects pulsed for a share of every 10 s, death and hurt triggers as a chance. Harming in armor mirrors the Healing gem: each survivable hit taken deals a share more.

| Effect | 1.0 means (worn) | s = 0.05 | s = 0.10 | s = 0.25 | s = 0.50 | s = 0.75 | s = 0.95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Healing gem (in armor)

When the wearer takes damage from an attack or a fall and survives it, they instantly get back a fraction of the health that hit took. A killing blow still kills. Its own curve: `heal = 0.25 x (total / 0.95)^0.7`, so the best build returns exactly 25% and early gems are flattened upward to stay noticeable. On a weapon it heals the target, as a charged strike (below).

**Why 25% at the very best:** it works like 25% less damage from survivable hits, between Resistance I (20%) and Resistance II (40%), and far below the Resistance gem's own best (76%) or full Protection IV armor (64%). It never stops a one-shot, never heals outside a fight, and is always a net loss (you can't farm it with fall damage). A Healing II potion gives 8 HP at once; at 25% the wearer must take 32 HP of hits, about one and a half health bars, to get that much back. So it is a comfort in long fights, not a second health bar.

## In a weapon: what one hit gives the target

A weapon holds 2 gems. Swords, axes, maces, tridents and spears apply the gem's effects to what they hit; bows and crossbows turn each fired arrow into its tipped form carrying them (picked up again, it's a plain arrow). Each hit **refreshes** the effect, it never stacks. A real tipped arrow fired from a gemmed bow: the stronger effect applies (higher strength wins, then longer duration), never both. Harmful gems are what weapons are for; a beneficial gem on a weapon buffs the target (pointless, but allowed).

**Per hit:** the weapon's strength `s` is shared equally between how hard and how long: potency = s^0.5 of the 1.0 level, duration = s^0.5 of the 1.0 duration, so potency x duration = s. On/off harmful effects (Wind Charged, Weaving, Oozing, Infested, Glowing, Levitation, Blindness, Nausea, Darkness) put it all into duration. Harmful effects with no tipped arrow are anchored on their strongest vanilla source: a hit source (wither skeleton, spectral arrow, shulker bullet) at its full duration, any other source (food, a mob's pulse or spell) at tipped-arrow scale, 1/8. Beneficial effects with no potion: the strongest vanilla source at arrow scale (Absorption: the enchanted golden apple), or, with none, a 3:00 potion's tipped arrow (22.5 s, proposal). Harming and Healing are charged strikes: the first hit or arrow after a 10 s charge deals s x 12 magic damage, or heals the target s x 8 HP, so a bow can't fire them without limit.

## Drawbacks

A drawback roll (tier 1's weak drawback alone, or tier 3's strongest + weak drawback) is a fixed size: **10% of the strongest vanilla level** of that effect, whatever the potion, Infusion level or gear (a better gem shouldn't hurt more). More drawbacks of the same effect add less and less and never pass 20%, which is below vanilla's weakest level of every drawback effect. So they sting, but never as much as a real potion of it. It goes where the gem's main effect goes: in armor, on the wearer while worn; in a weapon, on the target for 3 s, refreshed by each hit (a beneficial gem's harmful drawback on a weapon therefore lands on the target too).

| Drawback | Rolls on | 1.0 means (vanilla) | 1 drawback (0.100) | 2 drawbacks (0.150) | 3 drawbacks (0.175) | 12 drawbacks (0.200) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Slowness | beneficial gems | Slowness IV (strong Slowness potion): movement speed -60% | -6.0% speed | -9.0% speed | -10.5% speed | -12.0% speed |
| Weakness | beneficial gems | Weakness I: attack damage -4 (only level) | -0.40 attack damage | -0.60 attack damage | -0.70 attack damage | -0.80 attack damage |
| Mining Fatigue | beneficial gems | Mining Fatigue III (elder guardian): mining x0.027, attack speed -30% | mining x0.70, attack speed -3.0% | mining x0.58, attack speed -4.5% | mining x0.53, attack speed -5.3% | mining x0.49, attack speed -6.0% |
| Hunger | beneficial gems | Hunger III (pufferfish): exhaustion +0.015 per tick | extra hunger: 1 food point per 133 s | extra hunger: 1 food point per 89 s | extra hunger: 1 food point per 76 s | extra hunger: 1 food point per 67 s |
| Bad Luck | beneficial gems | Bad Luck I: luck -1 | -0.10 luck | -0.15 luck | -0.18 luck | -0.20 luck |
| Speed | harmful gems | Speed II: movement speed +40% (0.2 per level, add_multiplied_total) | +4.0% speed | +6.0% speed | +7.0% speed | +8.0% speed |
| Regeneration | harmful gems | Regeneration II: 1 HP every 25 ticks (interval 50 >> level) = 0.8 HP/s | 0.08 HP/s (1 heart per 25.0 s) | 0.12 HP/s (1 heart per 16.7 s) | 0.14 HP/s (1 heart per 14.3 s) | 0.16 HP/s (1 heart per 12.5 s) |
| Resistance (from Turtle Master) | harmful gems | Resistance IV (strong Turtle Master): damage taken -80% ((level x 5) / 25) | damage taken -8.0% | damage taken -12.0% | damage taken -14.0% | damage taken -16.0% |
| Jump Boost | harmful gems | Jump Boost II: jump velocity +0.2 (0.1 per level) and safe fall distance +2 (1 per level) | jump 1.37 blocks (vanilla 1.25), safe fall 3.2 | jump 1.42 blocks (vanilla 1.25), safe fall 3.3 | jump 1.45 blocks (vanilla 1.25), safe fall 3.4 | jump 1.48 blocks (vanilla 1.25), safe fall 3.4 |

### How each effect is made partial

| Effect | Implementation | Source (26.3) |
|---|---|---|
| Speed | Attribute modifier on movement_speed, +0.4 x s, add_multiplied_total (exact). | MobEffects.SPEED |
| Strength | Attribute modifier on attack_damage, +6 x s, add_value (exact). | MobEffects.STRENGTH |
| Jump Boost | Attribute modifiers: jump_strength +0.2 x s and safe_fall_distance +2 x s. (Vanilla adds the jump boost after the block jump factor; the attribute is scaled by it, so it is a little weaker on honey.) | MobEffects.JUMP_BOOST, LivingEntity.getJumpBoostPower, Attributes.JUMP_STRENGTH 0.42 |
| Regeneration | Tick handler: heal 0.8 x s / 20 HP per tick while hurt (LivingEntity.heal takes floats). Not a MobEffectInstance, because vanilla levels are whole numbers. | RegenerationMobEffect |
| Resistance (from Turtle Master) | Damage hook (mixin at LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb, beside vanilla's resistance), x (1 - 0.8 x s), skipping bypasses_resistance damage. | LivingEntity.getDamageAfterMagicAbsorb, Potions.STRONG_TURTLE_MASTER |
| Fire Resistance | On/off made partial: fire-tagged damage (is_fire) x (1 - s) through the damage hook, and burning_time attribute -s (add_multiplied_total) so fire also goes out sooner. | LivingEntity (is_fire + FIRE_RESISTANCE), Entity lava 4.0, Attributes.BURNING_TIME |
| Water Breathing | On/off made partial with the vanilla oxygen_bonus attribute (what Respiration uses): bonus = s / (1 - s), so each air tick is kept with chance s. Pure attribute, exact. | LivingEntity.decreaseAirSupply, Entity.getMaxAirSupply 300 |
| Night Vision | On/off made partial on the client: set the lightmap's nightVisionEffectIntensity to s (mixin at LightmapRenderStateExtractor, where vanilla writes GameRenderer.nightVisionScale). Vanilla already renders fractional values during its end-fade. | GameRenderer.nightVisionScale, LightmapRenderStateExtractor |
| Invisibility | Stealth, not a see-through body: the vanilla mob_visibility item component on each gemmed piece (pieces multiply, so each gets total^(1/n)), plus waypoint_transmit_range -s. Data only. | LivingEntity.getVisibilityPercent, item/component/MobVisibility, MobEffects.INVISIBILITY |
| Slow Falling | On/off made partial: while falling, gravity 0.08 - 0.07 x s (mixin at LivingEntity.getEffectiveGravity, where vanilla checks slow falling) and fall_damage_multiplier -s. | LivingEntity.getEffectiveGravity, Attributes.GRAVITY 0.08 |
| Luck | Attribute modifier on luck, +s (exact). | MobEffects.LUCK |
| Healing | After the wearer takes damage from an attack (an entity source) or a fall and survives it, heal that damage instance's health loss x the gem's fraction, at once. A killing blow still kills (the heal runs after the hit, only if the wearer is alive). Mixin after LivingEntity.actuallyHurt. Works the same on mobs. | LivingEntity.actuallyHurt, DamageTypeTags.IS_FALL, HealOrHarmMobEffect |
| Poison | Gem Poison mob effect (vanilla's icon and rules; potency in 1% steps): never below 1 HP, undead immune, milk clears it. | PoisonMobEffect, Potions.STRONG_POISON |
| Slowness | Gem Slowness mob effect: movement_speed -0.6 x potency (add_multiplied_total). As a drawback: the same modifier, permanent while worn. | MobEffects.SLOWNESS, Potions.STRONG_SLOWNESS |
| Weakness | Gem Weakness mob effect: attack_damage -4 x potency. As a drawback: the same modifier, permanent while worn. | MobEffects.WEAKNESS, Potions.LONG_WEAKNESS |
| Harming | Charged strike: the first hit or arrow after a 10 s charge deals +12 x s magic damage (HealOrHarmMobEffect.applyInstantaneousEffect). Undead are healed instead, as in vanilla. | HealOrHarmMobEffect |
| Wind Charged | The vanilla effect itself (it has one level), for a duration scaled by s. | WindChargedMobEffect, Potions.WIND_CHARGED |
| Weaving | The vanilla effect itself (it has one level), for a duration scaled by s. | WeavingMobEffect, Potions.WEAVING |
| Oozing | The vanilla effect itself (it has one level), for a duration scaled by s. | OozingMobEffect, Potions.OOZING |
| Infested | The vanilla effect itself (it has one level), for a duration scaled by s. | InfestedMobEffect, Potions.INFESTED |
| Haste | Attribute modifiers: block_break_speed +0.4 x s and attack_speed +0.2 x s (add_multiplied_total). | Player.getDestroySpeed, MobEffects.HASTE, BeaconBlockEntity |
| Absorption | max_absorption +16 x s, refilled to full 30 s after it was last hit. | AbsorptionMobEffect, Consumables.GOLDEN_APPLE / ENCHANTED_GOLDEN_APPLE |
| Health Boost | Attribute modifier on max_health, +8 x s (exact). | MobEffects.HEALTH_BOOST |
| Dolphin's Grace | On/off made partial: water slow-down 0.8 + 0.16 x s (mixin where travelInWater sets 0.96). | LivingEntity.travelInWater, DOLPHINS_GRACE_WATER_DRAG, Dolphin |
| Saturation | On/off made partial: food exhaustion x (1 - s) (mixin at FoodData.addExhaustion). Food still drains, just slower, so eating stays part of the game. | SaturationMobEffect, FoodData.addExhaustion, Blocks.DANDELION / BLUE_ORCHID |
| Conduit Power | On/off made partial, only while in water or rain: oxygen_bonus s / (1 - s), submerged_mining_speed raised by s of the way to 1.0, underwater fog s of the way to the conduit view. | ConduitBlockEntity, MobEffectUtil.hasWaterBreathing, Attributes.SUBMERGED_MINING_SPEED |
| Hero of the Village | Price hook beside vanilla's: the hero modifier 0.55 x s (mixin at Villager.updateSpecialPrices). Villagers' gifts stay vanilla-only (the effect itself). | Villager.updateSpecialPrices, Raid |
| Wither | Gem Wither mob effect (vanilla's icon; potency in 1% steps); it can kill, as vanilla's does. | WitherSkeleton.doHurtTarget, WitherMobEffect |
| Mining Fatigue | Gem Mining Fatigue mob effect: block_break_speed x 0.027^potency and attack_speed -0.3 x potency. As a drawback: the same, permanent while worn. | ElderGuardian, Player.getDestroySpeed |
| Hunger | Gem Hunger mob effect: causeFoodExhaustion(0.015 x potency) per tick (players only; mobs have no food). As a drawback: the same, permanent while worn. | HungerMobEffect, Consumables.PUFFERFISH / ROTTEN_FLESH |
| Glowing | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | SpectralArrow |
| Levitation | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | ShulkerBullet |
| Blindness | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | Illusioner, Blocks.AZURE_BLUET |
| Nausea | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | Consumables.PUFFERFISH |
| Darkness | The vanilla effect itself, for a duration scaled by s. Mostly felt by players (PvP, and gemmed mob gear hitting players). | Warden |
| Bad Luck | Attribute modifier on luck, -s. | MobEffects.UNLUCK |

Worn (armor) effects are attribute modifiers, data components or small tick and damage hooks, not potion effect instances: vanilla levels are whole numbers and their icons and timers would claim a full level. Hit-applied (weapon) effects, and weapon drawbacks on the target, are gem mob effects whose amplifier counts strength in 1% steps, with vanilla's icon and timer; a gem arrow carries one as its potion contents with a duration scale of 1. A gem and a drunk potion of the same effect don't add up: the stronger applies (open question).

## Checks (all passed)

- vanilla facts: 128 facts matched against build/mcsrc/26.3
- every ladder step (Infusion level, armor, weapon material, run, grade, potion variant) is at least +4% on the one below; Infusion VI (nether star) and netherite are the only bests; each tier's odds add up to 100%
- a gem's own strength reaches 1.0 only from the strongest potion or source item + lingering form + tier 3 + Infusion VI (nether star), for every craftable gem; a found-only gem is perfect only from ominous loot at Infusion VI and tier 3
- all 40 status effects in 26.3 are classified: 30 craftable gems, 5 found-only gems, 1 drawback-only, 4 not gems
- 804,837 armor layouts x gem counts enumerated: only full contiguous netherite with 12 gems reaches 0.95; next best 0.922
- 27,335 weapons x gem combinations enumerated: only a netherite weapon with 2 perfect gems reaches 0.95; next best weapon or gem count with perfect gems 0.883
- from the best armor build and the best weapon build, every single step down (potion, base, tier, material, run, one gem fewer, a material-less weapon) loses at least 0.025
- weakest single armor gem (normal potion, Infusion I, tier 1, lone leather piece) = 0.034; early armor kit (iron set, 4 Infusion II tier-1 gems) = 0.155-0.193; weakest weapon gem (wooden sword, Infusion I, tier 1) = 0.123; early weapon (iron sword, 1 Infusion II tier-1 gem) = 0.150-0.188
- stacking: 25,000 random armor and weapon stacks never pass 0.95 x their strongest gem; adding a gem never lowers a total; 12 tier-1 armor gems lose to 4 tier-3 in every set, and 2 tier-1 weapon gems lose to 1 tier-3 on every weapon
- every one of the 35 gems has a worn (armor) and a hit-applied (weapon) form; every worn mapping rises with strength and stays short of the vanilla level at the cap
- healing: best build returns 25% of each non-lethal hit (never a whole hit, so taking damage is always a net loss); early kit 7.0%; every step down from the best loses at least 0.5 points; the curve is flatter than linear
- drawbacks: one is 10% of the strongest vanilla level, any number of one effect stays under 20%, below vanilla's level I for every drawback effect; poison, wither, harming and the rest of the never-drawback list never roll
- rolls: each of the 35 gems has one roll table; 'other' pools 14-17 effects, all the main effect's kind and never itself; drawback pools 3-5 effects, all the opposite kind, none on the never-drawback list, and none a direct opposite (13 inverse pairs, the owner's 12 included)
- weapons: per hit, potency and duration both rise with strength, for every gem; at the best build every effect stays under the strongest vanilla tipped arrow, so a real strong tipped arrow always wins the 'stronger applies' comparison and a gem arrow beats the weaker ones

## Open questions for the owner

1. Cap at 0.95 (5% short of the strongest vanilla level)? yes / no (0.90 would make the gap easier to feel).
2. Gold armor and gold weapons: (a) chainmail-level factor 0.83 (model), (b) a magic bonus up to diamond-level 0.93, echoing gold's high enchantability.
3. Turtle helmet counts as its own material (iron-level, always a run of 1)? yes / no.
4. Resistance's 1.0: (a) Resistance IV from strong Turtle Master, 80% less damage (the rule as written; gems up to 76%), (b) Resistance II, the beacon level, 40% (gems up to 38%).
5. Turtle Master gems also carry Turtle Master's Slowness? yes / no.
6. Healing gem in armor returns at most 25% of each survivable hit (early iron kit about 7%)? yes / no.
7. Drawback size: one drawback is 10% of the strongest vanilla level, many of one effect stay under 20%, the same whatever the gem or gear? yes / no.
8. Poison and wither never roll as a beneficial gem's drawback (its pool stays Slowness, Weakness, Mining Fatigue, Hunger, Bad Luck, minus the direct opposite: 4-5 candidates)? yes / no.
9. A harmful gem's drawback rolls from Speed, Regeneration, Resistance and Jump Boost (Jump Boost is new, so no harmful gem is left with only 2), minus the direct opposite? yes / no.
10. Conduit Power and Mining Fatigue count as direct opposites (Conduit Power's underwater mining is the conduit's Haste)? yes / no.
11. Jump Boost, Resistance, Health Boost, Absorption, Fire Resistance, Water Breathing and Dolphin's Grace have no direct opposite (nothing excluded from their drawbacks)? yes / no.
12. Healing, Harming and Hero of the Village are main-effect-only, never an 'other' roll? yes / no.
13. Harming in armor mirrors the Healing gem (each survivable hit taken deals up to 25% more)? (a) yes (model), (b) a magic-damage pulse every 10 s instead.
14. Harmful on/off gems in armor (Blindness, Darkness, Nausea, Glowing, Levitation) are on for a share of every 10 s, by strength? yes / no (the alternative is always on).
15. Beneficial gems with no potion or timed source (Haste, Health Boost, Saturation, Dolphin's Grace, Conduit Power, Hero of the Village), on a weapon: the target gets the effect for up to 22.5 s, as if from a 3:00 potion's tipped arrow? yes / no.
16. Weapon material is a strength factor, like armor (wood ... netherite)? yes / no.
17. Bows, crossbows, tridents and maces (no material): (a) diamond-level 0.93, so only netherite weapons reach the cap (model), (b) netherite-level 1.00.
18. Weapon strength per hit: (a) shared between potency and duration (model), (b) all into potency, always the strongest arrow's duration.
19. Harming and Healing on a weapon strike once per 10 s charge (not every hit)? yes / no.
20. The weapon's 1.0 is the strongest vanilla tipped arrow (Poison II 2.7 s, Slowness IV 2.5 s), not the drunk potion (Poison II 21.6 s)? yes / no.
21. Wither's 1.0: (a) the wither skeleton's hit, Wither I for 10 s (model: a weapon matches a weapon), (b) the Wither boss's skull, Wither II for 10 s.
22. Wither gems from the wither rose? yes / no (the alternative is found-only, from Wither-fight loot).
23. Saturation gems: (a) from suspicious stew of dandelion, golden dandelion or blue orchid (model), (b) from a golden dandelion itself, (c) found-only.
24. Blindness gems from suspicious stew of azure bluet or open eyeblossom, and Nausea gems from pufferfish? yes / no.
25. Darkness gems from echo shards (ancient cities)? yes / no (the alternative is found-only, in ancient cities).
26. Conduit Power gems from a heart of the sea, and Dolphin's Grace gems from a nautilus shell? yes / no.
27. Haste, Health Boost, Luck and Hero of the Village are found-only, in the places listed? yes / no.
28. Hero of the Village gems: villager trades up to 52% cheaper at the best build, while worn? yes / no (a permanent discount is strong; the alternative is not a gem).
29. Mining Fatigue gems come only from elder guardians (a rare extra drop) and ominous vaults? yes / no.
30. Bad Omen, Trial Omen, Raid Omen and Breath of the Nautilus are not gems? yes / no.
31. A gem and a drunk potion of the same effect: the stronger applies, they don't add? yes / no.
32. Undead follow vanilla's inversion (a healing gem hurts a zombie wearer, harming heals an undead target; undead ignore poison and regeneration)? yes / no.
33. Invisibility gems give stealth only (mobs notice you later, hidden on the locator bar), never a see-through body? yes / no.
34. Enchant odds as proposed (tier 1: 50/50; tier 2: medium alone 50%, + weak other 50%; tier 3: alone 40%, + weak other 30%, + medium other 15%, + weak drawback 15%)? yes / no.
